charts.title: Total Equity vs. Owners' Equity vs. Perpetual Notes
Total Profit vs. Profit Attributable to Owners

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity (owners' share) is assets less liabilities less minority interests; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For China Railway Group Limited (CREC): this line is the owners'-only slice -- see "Capital Structure" below for how much of the balance sheet's equity actually belongs to minority holders and perpetual noteholders instead.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

equityStructure.title: Total equity vs. owners' equity vs. perpetual notes
equityStructure.content:
Total equity includes minority interests (non-controlling interests, or NCI) from consolidated subsidiaries; shareholders' equity is the owners'-only slice. Perpetual notes are a subset of shareholders' equity -- IFRS classifies them as equity because they have no fixed maturity, but economically they carry a fixed coupon and are callable, much like debt.

For China Railway Group Limited (CREC): CREC consolidates large PPP and infrastructure-concession subsidiaries, many only partly owned, so the gap between total and owners' equity is substantial (FY2025: RMB540,450m total vs RMB370,915m owners' -- a RMB169,535m minority claim). Of that owners' RMB370,915m, RMB52,794m (14%) is perpetual notes, not ordinary equity a shareholder can claim pro-rata on liquidation or that compounds like retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Total-vs-owners' gap widening (minority interests growing faster than the parent's share)
  • Perpetual notes growing as a share of shareholders' equity -- it dilutes the quality, not just the quantity, of book value
  • Any step-change around a new PPP concession consolidating or a perpetual note issuance/redemption

profitAttribution.title: Total profit vs. profit attributable to owners
profitAttribution.content:
Total profit includes the minority interests' share of consolidated subsidiaries' earnings; net income (attributable to owners) is what is left for CREC's own shareholders after that cut.

For China Railway Group Limited (CREC): the minority share of profit here is proportionally larger than the minority share of equity in some years, since partly-owned PPP/concession subsidiaries can be more or less profitable than the wholly-owned core contracting business. FY2025 total profit was RMB26,347m against RMB22,892m attributable to owners -- minority holders took roughly 13% of the group's earnings.

What to watch:

  • The minority share of profit rising faster than the minority share of equity (new consolidations earning above or below the group average)
  • Owners' net income growing slower than total profit -- dilution of the group's earnings by minority claims, not by share count

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For China Railway Group Limited (CREC): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For China Railway Group Limited (CREC): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For China Railway Group Limited (CREC): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For China Railway Group Limited (CREC): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For China Railway Group Limited (CREC): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For China Railway Group Limited (CREC): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For China Railway Group Limited (CREC): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For China Railway Group Limited (CREC): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
